name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Smartphone Delivery & Arbitrary Return Cancellation
case_dossier.summary: The user purchased a Samsung Galaxy smartphone for Rs 26,999, which arrived with a manufacturing defect. Although a replacement request was raised within 24 hours of delivery and a technician verified the hardware defect within the 7-day window, customer support arbitrarily cancelled the return citing expiration of the window.

timeline.event: Ordered Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on the e-commerce app.
Smartphone was delivered to the user.
Screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working; user noticed the defect.
Raised a replacement request on the e-commerce app.
Technician sent by the app inspected the phone, confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and took a signature on the job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request claiming the 7-day return window expired on 21st November and directed the user to a brand service center.

evidence_needed: Unboxing video or photos showing the defect immediately upon delivery (if available)
Written refusal email or chat log from customer support showing the cancellation reason
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary evidence including tax invoice, delivery receipt, and an official technician job sheet confirming the manufacturing defect.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a strong consumer protection claim because your smartphone arrived with a verified manufacturing defect and your return request was initiated on time. Under Indian consumer law, selling defective goods and arbitrarily cancelling a valid return amounts to unfair trade practices and deficiency in service. You can successfully seek a full refund or replacement, along with compensation, through consumer dispute forums without needing a lawyer.

governing_laws.relevance: Defines you as a consumer since you purchased goods for consideration.
Covers manufacturing defects and shortcomings in product quality.
Defines deficiency in service for arbitrary cancellation of return and poor customer support.
Classifies deceptive practices and refusal to refund/replace within stipulated timelines as an unfair trade practice.
Establishes product manufacturer liability for manufacturing defects regardless of negligence.
Provides the statutory right and electronic filing mechanism for a consumer complaint before the District Commission.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action
action_options.details: Serve a formal Legal Demand Notice to the e-commerce platform and seller enclosing your tax invoice, delivery receipt, and the technician inspection job sheet.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: Lodge a formal complaint on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) toll-free number 1915 or via consumerhelpline.gov.in. Note: DLSA helpline 15100 provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Consumer Commission Petition
action_options.details: File an electronic consumer complaint online on e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in) attaching your order invoice, defect photos, technician job sheet, and customer support chat logs.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Consumer Commissions are designed for self-representation, allowing you to argue your case and present evidence personally without hiring a licensed advocate.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE**

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post with Acknowledgement Due (AD) / Registered Email 
**DATE:** 09/11/2026 

**FROM:** 
[Complainant / Consumer Name] 
[Complainant Address Line 1] 
[Complainant Address Line 2] 
Phone: [Complainant Phone Number] 
Email: [Complainant Email Address] 

**TO:** 
1. **The Grievance Officer / Managing Director** 
 [E-Commerce Platform Name / Seller Name] 
 [Company Address Line 1] 
 [Company Address Line 2] 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR DEFECTIVE PRODUCT DELIVERY, ARBITRARY CANCELLATION OF RETURN REQUEST, DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE, AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES UNDER THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019.**

---

Under instructions from my client, the undersigned submits as under:

1. That my client is a consumer as defined under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased goods for consideration through your e-commerce platform.

2. **RECITALS OF FACTS AND TIMELINE:**
 - **10th November 2024:** My client placed an online order on your e-commerce platform for a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth **Rs. 26,999/-** (Rupees Twenty-Six Thousand Nine Hundred and Ninety-Nine Only) against Tax Invoice No. [Invoice Number].
 - **14th November 2024:** The said smartphone was delivered to my client.
 - **Within 24 hours of delivery:** Upon unboxing and setting up the device, my client noticed a severe manufacturing hardware defect, wherein the screen started flickering with green lines and the touch screen stopped working entirely.
 - **15th November 2024:** Immediately, well within any applicable return and replacement windows, my client raised a formal replacement request on your e-commerce application.
 - **21st November 2024:** An authorized technician sent by your platform physically inspected the smartphone at my client's premises, independently verified and confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and collected my client's signature on the official technician inspection job sheet.
 - **23rd November 2024:** Despite the technician's verification, your customer support arbitrarily and wrongfully cancelled my client's return request, falsely claiming that the 7-day return window had expired on 21st November 2024, and improperly directed my client to approach a brand service center instead of honoring your platform's return/replacement policy.

3. **VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS:**
 - The delivery of a defective smartphone constitutes a direct violation of product quality standards under Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
 - The arbitrary cancellation of a validly raised return request and failure to provide proper after-sales redressal constitutes a gross "deficiency in service" under Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
 - Refusing to honor a valid replacement/refund for a defective product verified by your own technician amounts to an "unfair trade practice" under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
 - Under Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the product manufacturer and platform are liable for manufacturing defects.

4. **EVIDENCE HELD BY CLIENT:**
 - Tax invoice
 - Delivery receipt
 - Technician inspection job sheet copy confirming the manufacturing defect
 - Customer support chat screenshots

---

### **DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION**

Through this notice, my client hereby calls upon you to fulfill the following demands within **15 days** from the receipt of this notice:

1. Arrange for an immediate pickup and process a **full refund of Rs. 26,999/-** (or a brand-new replacement unit as originally requested) for the defective Samsung Galaxy smartphone.
2. Cease and desist from engaging in arbitrary cancellations of verified return requests and unfair trade practices.

---

**WARNING OF LEGAL ACTION:**

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE THAT if you fail to comply with the above demands within the stipulated **15-day** rectification window, my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings. This shall include filing a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate statutory **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** via the e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in), as well as lodging a grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) platform, seeking a full refund, statutory compensation for mental agony and harassment, and litigation costs, entirely at your sole risk, cost, and peril.

*(Note: For free legal guidance and information regarding your consumer rights, you may contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline at **15100**).*

---

Sincerely,

*(Signature)* 
**[Complainant / Consumer Name]** 
(Acting on behalf of self) 

---

### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY:**
1. Copy of Tax Invoice
2. Copy of Delivery Receipt
3. Copy of Technician Inspection Job Sheet
4. Screenshots of Customer Support Chats

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Daakhil.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sir/madam, why are you threatening with consumer helpline and all that big-big legal English? See, our system automatically cancelled the return because the automated barcode scan updated after 7 days. Technician report is fine, but company internal policy is final, na? Okay, okay, don't shout—let me check with my senior manager if we can give you a store voucher instead of cash refund.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You brilliantly cited specific sections of the Consumer Protection Act 2019 (Section 2(11) for deficiency in service and Section 84) along with concrete proof like the technician report.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Do not accept a store voucher if you want a full cash refund. Hold your ground on the monetary refund to your original payment method.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: I reject the store voucher; as per RBI guidelines and Consumer Protection Act, I demand an immediate full refund to my original payment source, or I proceed with my formal complaint.
